analysis:
The PR adds only documentation: changelog.d/serving-stalls.md (new, lines 1-5) and docs/architecture/hardware-support.md (mermaid load-gate nodes at lines 298-299 and a new paragraph at roughly lines 338-358). No executable code, wire protocol, key custody, attestation, authorization or billing logic is changed in the supplied units.

The documented behavior has two parts. The proactive MLX buffer-cache sweep is now gated on 5 s of whole-Mac idleness or on admission-headroom pressure. Paged KV pools also retain up to 1/8 of the slot grant (max 2 GiB) of free 64 MiB segments across requests. These segments are described as uncommitted and are dropped on refusal, on memory pressure, or after 30 s idle. New segments wrap zero-fill-on-demand host pages.

Security-relevant observations, none of which is an observed regression in the supplied evidence:
- Retained KV segments hold reusable GPU/host memory across requests. This relates to T-028 (residual inference data in GPU memory) and A-001. The docs say segments are reinstalled for the next admission instead of being zero-filled by device fills. With host zero pages, new segments are zeroed, but the evidence does not show whether a reinstalled retained segment is re-zeroed before reuse by a different tenant. The code is not supplied, so I cannot verify that. T-028 already accepts same-process residual memory, and the provider already shares a single prefix cache across tenants (T-041), so this is a question for the code reviewer, not a finding.
- A skipped device fill could change the timing profile, but I cannot establish a new oracle from docs alone.
- A retained pool counted as reclaimable by the load gates could affect availability (T-010, T-029). The paths are ProviderLoop.evictUntilAvailable, evictUntilNemotronSuperFits, StandaloneServer.ensureMemoryHeadroomForLoad and StartupPreloader.reclaimBeforeSkip, and none are in the supplied evidence.
- The changelog says DARKBLOOM_TTFT_* rollback env vars are forwarded by `darkbloom start` to launchd-managed providers. This is an operator-controlled tuning surface, not a privilege boundary.

The implementing Swift code (CBv2RetainedKVSegments, KVPoolReclaimer, GlobalKVCacheBudget.directChargeRefusalSignal) was not supplied. The next pass should check zeroing of reused segments, the gating of the 2 GiB cap, and the memory accounting race with the load gates.
